newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia pushes for farm trade reform at meeting.
newsitem.headline: Australia pushes for farm trade reform at meeting.

text.p: Australia will push for renewed efforts to cut barriers to farm trade during a meeting of the Cairns Group of agricultural free traders this week, Australian officials said on Thursday.

Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer, the group's chairman, would lobby the 15 country bloc to push for agriculture to be a priority in the next round of world trade talks, due to begin by 2000, Australia's trade negotiations chief Geoff Raby told reporters.
The Cairns Group will hold its annual ministerial conference in Rio de Janeiro on Thursday and Friday.
Raby said the Cairns Group played a vital role in bringing agriculture under world trade rules in the Uruguay round of General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) talks in the early 1990s.
Those talks agreed to convert non-tariff barriers against rural exports to tariffs as a prelude to further liberalisation.
"In a sense we have got ourselves up to the top of one mountain, but there's plenty of other peaks on the horizon," Raby said.
Australian exporters still faced substantial barriers, particularly in fast growing Asian markets.
"There are some very high peaks in tariffs," said Raby, citing rice in Japan and South Korea and processed food in South East Asia.
The Cairns Group conference is expected to focus on ways of pressing countries to meet their Uruguay Round obligations.
The group will also discuss efforts by several countries, including including China, Russia and Saudi Arabia, to join the World Trade Organisation.
